bihar_raw_news.title: 147 litres milk, 90 kg paneer destroyed during food safety raids in Bihar - CNBC TV18
bihar_raw_news.content: 147 litres milk, 90 kg paneer destroyed during food safety raids in Bihar In Hajipur, officials destroyed 72 kg of paneer after detecting starch adulteration. The paneer, seized from two establishments, was destroyed and a sample was sent for laboratory testing, the statement said. By PTI September 12, 2026, 9:16:27 PM IST (Published) 2 Min Read Food safety officials destroyed 147 litres of milk and 90 kg of paneer after detecting adulteration or expiry during raids in Patna, Hajipur and Darbhanga in Bihar, officials said on Saturday. The officials also collected samples of food products for laboratory testing, they said. The raids were conducted as part of a statewide drive against food adulteration and violations of food safety standards, on the directions of the state health secretary-cum-food safety commissioner Kumar Ravi. "Food safety and people's health cannot be compromised at any cost. Food business operators must ensure that only safe and standard products are supplied," Ravi said, according to a department statement. In Hajipur, officials destroyed 72 kg of paneer after detecting starch adulteration. The paneer, seized from two establishments, was destroyed and a sample was sent for laboratory testing, the statement said. At Benipur in Darbhanga district, officials found 21 litres of expired milk and 18 kg of spoiled paneer at a milk parlour and destroyed them on the spot, it said. In Patna's Fatuha, around 126 litres of milk was destroyed after formalin was detected in a sample collected from a dairy, officials said. A joint team of the food safety department, drug inspector, AYUSH directorate and police also inspected a food supplements manufacturing facility in Fatuha and collected samples for testing. No objectionable substances were found at the facility, officials said. Continue Reading

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar floods worsen, nearly 48 lakh people affected | Daily Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 12, 2026 Bihar flood situation remains grim, over 48 lakh affected Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Press Trust of India Source: PTI The flood situation in Bihar deteriorated on Saturday, with the number of affected people increasing to nearly 48.22 lakh across 15 districts, while several rivers, including the Ganga, were flowing above the danger levels. The Water Resources Department (WRD) cautioned against sudden and rapid riverbank erosion, and directed its officials to maintain close vigil at vulnerable locations. Due to the rise in water levels of several rivers, approximately 48.22 lakh people in 574 gram panchayats across 87 blocks in 15 districts have been affected by the floods, the Disaster Management Department said in a statement issued on Saturday. The flood-hit districts are Patna, Bhojpur, Saran, Vaishali, Bhagalpur, Begusarai, Buxar, Samastipur, Munger, Katihar, Lakhisarai, Khagaria, Purnia, Madhepura and Araria. The count of flood-affected people was 47.33 lakh on Friday evening. The government also instructed officials to ensure prompt reporting of any erosion incident and to keep adequate resources readily available at vulnerable locations. Incessant rain in Bihar, coupled with downpours in catchment areas of Nepal, has caused several rivers and streams to swell, officials said. The state has recorded 108.8 mm of rainfall in September so far, about 20 per cent above normal, they said. The Disaster Management Department said the Ganga was flowing at 36.48 metres at Sultanganj in Bhagalpur at 6 am on Saturday, 1.98 metres above the danger level, though the water level was receding. The water levels of the Gandak at Dumariaghat, the Kosi at Baltara and Kursela, the Burhi Gandak at Khagaria, the Ganga at Digha, Gandhi Ghat, Hathidah, Bhagalpur, Kahalgaon and Munger, the Punpun at Sripalpur, the Bagmati at Benibad, and the Ghaghra at Darauli and Gangpur Siswan were flowing above the danger marks, the Water Resources Department said. It stated that a sudden reduction in water levels could increase the risk of bank erosion, posing a threat to vulnerable stretches of riverbanks and embankments. The department officials have been directed to immediately inspect any location showing signs of sudden erosion, bank collapse, or rapid movement of the river current towards the bank, and to initiate necessary preventive and protective measures without delay. A total of 1,248 community kitchens are being operated in various districts for flood-affected people. In addition, 13 relief camps remain functional. In these facilities, arrangements for accommodation, food, medical care and other essential items have been made for 12,260 flood-affected people, the Disaster Management Department said. So far, approximately 3.53 lakh polythene sheets, 59,500 dry-ration packets and 1,400 food packets have been distributed among flood-hit people. A total of 1,794 boats are being operated to facilitate evacuation and transportation, it said, adding that so far, 11,424 quintals of animal fodder have been distributed. In view of floods and to ensure prompt relief and rescue operations, 27 SDRF (State Disaster Response Force) teams and 10 of the NDRF (National Disaster Response Force) have been deployed in various districts.

bihar_raw_news.title: Unit-II (660 MW) of SJVN's Buxar Thermal Power Project Successfully Achieves Commercial ...
bihar_raw_news.content: NEWS September 12, 2026 admin Sh. Bhupender Gupta, Chairman & Managing Director, SJVN, informed that SJVN has successfully achieved Commercial Operation Date (COD) of Unit-II (660 MW) of 1320 MW Buxar Thermal Power Project on 12.09.2026. Sh. Bhupender Gupta expressed gratitude to Central and State Governments, Ministry of Power and other key Ministries and Departments for their constant guidance and support. He also appreciated collective commitment, dedication and perseverance of SJVN employees and all stakeholders who have directly or indirectly contributed to achievement of this significant milestone. On this occasion, Sh. Ajay Kumar Sharma, Director (Personnel), Sh. Parthajit De, Director (Finance) and Sh. Rajesh Kumar Chandel, Director (Projects) congratulated all employees and associated stakeholders on this historic achievement. With commissioning of Unit-II, both units of Buxar Thermal Power Project are commercially operational, bringing full 1320 MW capacity into operation. This is also first thermal power project of SJVN to become fully operational. The 1320 MW (2×660 MW) Buxar Thermal Power Project, located at Chausa in Buxar District, Bihar, has been implemented by SJVN Thermal Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of SJVN. Earlier, Unit-I (660 MW) of the project was virtually inaugurated by Hon’ble Prime Minister Sh. Narendra Modi on August 22, 2025 and had achieved Commercial Operation Date on November 14,2025. Buxar Thermal Power Project is based on state-of-the-art supercritical technology and is equipped with advanced emission-control systems, ensuring higher operational efficiency and reduced environmental impact. Developed at a total investment of ₹ 13,756.56 crore (Revised at June 2025 price level), project is expected to generate 9828.72 million units of electricity annually at 85% Plant Load Factor. Of the total power generated, 85% has been allocated to Bihar under a long-term Power Purchase Agreement. The project will substantially enhance power availability in Bihar and Eastern Region, help reduce peak-hour shortages and contribute to strengthening energy security. During the construction phase, the project engaged approximately 65,000 workers across various stages of development. Project has created substantial direct and indirect employment and economic opportunities particularly for local communities and this multiplier effect is expected to continue during operational phase as well. SJVN has also undertaken several community development initiatives in and around project area, with focus on education, healthcare, sanitation, access to safe drinking water, women empowerment and other areas of socio-economic development. Successful commercial operation of Unit-II represents not only a major milestone in strengthening India’s power generation capacity but also reflects SJVN’s steadfast commitment to energy security, regional development, employment generation and inclusive socio-economic progress.

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar hikes stipend for PG medical students
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar hikes stipend for PG medical students: 1st year to Rs 92,800, 2nd year Rs 1.02 lakh, 3rd year Rs 1.12 lakh Subscribe to Notifications Written By : Adity Saha Published On 2026-09-12 11:29 GMT | Update On 2026-09-12 12:33 GMT Patna: In a recent development, the Bihar State Health Department has increased the monthly stipend of postgraduate (PG) medical students serving in government medical colleges and hospitals across the state. As per the decision, the monthly stipend for first-year PG students has been increased from Rs 82,000 to Rs 92,800. For second-year students, it has been raised from Rs 90,200 to Rs 1,02,000 per month. Third-year PG medical students will now receive Rs 1,12,200 per month, up from their previous stipend of Rs 99,220. The revised rates will take effect retroactively from January 1, 2026, according to an official statement posted on the social media platform X. Also read- Doctors oppose Bihar govt's ban on private practice While announcing the revised stipend structure, the Bihar Health Department in the X post said that the increase is aimed at providing better financial support to PG medical students as they play an active role in patient care and hospital services while working under the supervision of senior doctors. "A major boon for PG medical students in Bihar, with a significant increase in the stipend for PG students. An important decision by the Bihar government. PG students who play an active role in patient treatment and hospital services under the supervision of senior doctors. They will receive better economic cooperation and encouragement for quality human resources in the field of medical education," the health department further stated in the post. “PG students are future specialist doctors and have an important role in the state’s healthcare system. The increase in stipend would encourage them and help create a better environment for medical education,” Bihar Health Minister Nishant Kumar said, according to the statement, PTI reported. The state government’s objective is not only to increase the number of medical institutions but also to develop specialised medical manpower capable of providing better and quality healthcare services to the people, he added. This comes a day after the state government increased the monthly honoraria to contractual professors, associate professors, assistant professors, and resident doctors. Medical Dialogues had reported that the monthly honorarium for contractual professors has been increased from Rs 1.80 lakh to Rs 2.07 lakh. Contractual associate professors will now receive Rs 1.55 lakh, up from Rs 1.35 lakh, while the honorarium for assistant professors has been raised from Rs 1.10 lakh to Rs 1.25 lakh. The government has also revised the monthly honorarium for senior residents and tutors to Rs 1.15 lakh. The honorarium for junior residents has been increased from Rs 65,000 to Rs 75,000. bihar_raw_news.title: Goat Rearing Scheme Brings Financial Stability to Gujarat's farmers - ANI News
bihar_raw_news.content: Goat Rearing Scheme Brings Financial Stability to Gujarat’s farmers Updated: 8 hours, 51 min ago A government livestock scheme is helping farmers in Gujarat build sustainable livelihoods. In Jamnagar’s Tamachal village, Hathabhai Chavaliya turned to goat rearing after struggling with employment and financial difficulties. With government support, he purchased 10 goats and one buck - and started a new livelihood for his family. The initiative has brought Hathabhai a regular source of income, greater financial stability and confidence. Under the Animal Husbandry Department’s goat-rearing scheme, beneficiaries receive assistance up to 1.20 lakh rupees for purchasing goats, along with support for fencing, shelter and fodder. Along with financial assistance, the government provides veterinary services to support livestock health and productivity. Such initiatives are encouraging rural families to take up livestock farming, create sustainable sources of income and move towards greater self-reliance. These initiatives reflect the government’s efforts to strengthen rural livelihoods by supporting livestock farmers at every stage. By promoting livestock farming and providing financial as well as veterinary support, the government is helping families build sustainable incomes and become self-reliant. bihar_raw_news.title: Monolithisch India bags quartzite stone block in Bihar for Rs 157 crore
bihar_raw_news.content: Agencies The company produces premixed ramming mass, a key refractory material used in induction furnaces by the secondary steel industry. New Delhi: Monolithisch India on Friday said it has secured a quartzite stone block in Nawada district through an e-auction conducted by Bihar's Mines and Geology Department for Rs 157 crore. The company produces premixed ramming mass, a key refractory material used in induction furnaces by the secondary steel industry. The acquisition marks the largest strategic milestone in the company's journey since inception and completes a significant step towards backward integration of its raw material supply chain, a company statement said. The block has been allotted for five years, with an approved mining capacity of 7,10,000 metric tonnes (MT) per annum, translating into a cumulative capacity of 35,50,000 MT over the lease period. The acquisition will provide greater control over the company's key raw material requirements and help hedge raw material prices for the next five years, as Monolithisch India expands its silica ramming mass manufacturing capacity. Live Events Consolidated group manufacturing capacity is expected to reach 5,76,000 MTPA. Subject to statutory approvals expected within 3-4 months, commercial operations are targeted to commence in February/March 2027. The Rs 157 crore consideration will be paid in tranches over five years in accordance with state government guidelines. Mining operations will be undertaken through experienced national mining contractors on a per-ton raising contract basis, limiting the company's direct infrastructure capital expenditure. A dedicated beneficiation and storage unit will also be established near the block to support quality management, R&D and product development. Harsh Tekriwal, Managing Director of Monolithisch India, said, "I am proud to announce that our backward integration is complete, with surplus raw material capacity, securing our needs that were supposed to grow rapidly with the commencement of our new greenfield project. The company is a major supplier of domestic integrated secondary steel clusters, especially in eastern and central India". Tekriwal is of the view that this strategic move will significantly strengthen the company's competitiveness in quality and cost in the coming years. This block belt was operational from 2015-2020, and the ore in this block was highly sought after by secondary steel cluster customers for its quality and consistency. This allotment will also accelerate the development of new products based on ore behaviour from a single, consistent supply source. He also said, "This acquisition is only the first step in our next phase of growth; we will pursue similar initiatives to secure raw materials before launching new product verticals". bihar_raw_news.title: RJD announces candidates for six seats ahead of Bihar MLC polls
bihar_raw_news.content: Politics 11 Sep, 2026 RJD announces candidates for six seats ahead of Bihar MLC polls Business To Business, Patna, 11 September 2026: The Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) has intensified preparations for the upcoming elections to eight seats in the Bihar Legislative Council, announcing candidates for six constituencies while discussions over the remaining two are still underway. The elections will be held for four Teachers' Constituency and four Graduates' Constituency seats. The terms of the sitting MLCs are scheduled to expire on November 16, 2026, with the election process expected to be announced in September. Unlike Assembly elections, the Teachers' and Graduates' constituencies have a specialised electorate. While political parties are preparing their candidates, a number of Independent candidates are also expected to enter the contest. According to a list issued by the office of RJD state president Mangnilal Mandal, the party has named Dr Sanjiv Kumar Singh as its candidate for the Patna Teachers' Constituency and Dilip Kumar for the Patna Graduates' Constituency. The party has also fielded Nitesh Kumar from the Kosi Graduates' Constituency, Anil Kumar Jha from the Darbhanga Graduates' Constituency, Prof. Jayram Yadav from the Saran Teachers' Constituency and Dr Rashmi Vinayak Gautam from the Tirhut Graduates' Constituency. The RJD said discussions are continuing over the selection of candidates for the two remaining seats. Their names will be announced after the party finalises the candidates. With the tenure of the sitting MLCs approaching its end, political parties have stepped up preparations across the eight constituencies. The RJD has already outlined its strategy for several key seats, particularly in the Patna Teachers' and Graduates' constituencies. Among the four Teachers' Constituency seats, Prof. Naval Kishore Yadav of the BJP represents Patna, Dr Madan Mohan Jha of the Congress represents Darbhanga, Afaque Ahmad, an Independent, represents Saran, and Sanjay Kumar Singh of the CPI represents Tirhut. In the four Graduates' Constituencies, Neeraj Kumar of the JD(U) represents Patna, Sarvesh Kumar, an Independent, represents Darbhanga, NK Yadav of the BJP represents Kosi, and Banshidhar Brajvasi, an Independent, represents Tirhut, and their tenure will be completed in November this year. The specialised nature of the electorate is expected to make the contests different from conventional Assembly elections. Among the Teachers' Constituencies, Patna has the largest voter base with 16,689 registered voters, followed by Saran with 10,800, Tirhut with 9,204 and Darbhanga with 8,967 voters. The Graduates' Constituencies have substantially larger electorates. Tirhut has approximately 1.35 lakh voters, followed by Kosi with around 1.34 lakh, Darbhanga with nearly 1.27 lakh and Patna with about 88,000 voters. Alongside established political parties, Independent candidates are also preparing to campaign among teachers and graduates in their respective constituencies. bihar_raw_news.content: High-level review meeting regarding preparations for 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan' concludes under chairmanship of Chief Secretary of Bihar ANI 11 Sep 2026, 22:29 GMT+10 Patna (Bihar) [India], September 11 (ANI): A high-level review meeting was held under the chairmanship of Bihar Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit to discuss the comprehensive preparations and successful implementation of the 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan' (Service Pledge Campaign), scheduled to take place from September 17 to October 17. According to a press release, Principal Secretaries and Secretaries from various state departments attended the meeting in person, while District Magistrates from all districts joined via video conferencing. During the review, the Chief Secretary assessed the department-wise status of all 13 key components of the campaign and directed officials to complete preparations in a time-bound manner. The release noted that the campaign will commence on the evening of September 17 with the 'Aashirwad ka Diya' (Lamp of Blessing) program, involving the collective lighting of lamps in every household across the state and at a minimum of 10 prominent or symbolic public locations in each district. To facilitate this, lamps will be distributed to beneficiaries through Jeevika, urban local bodies, and the Public Distribution System. Additionally, between September 17 and October 7, painting and speech competitions based on the theme 'Viksit Bharat Sankalp' (Developed India Pledge) will be organised in all government and private schools under the 'Seva Chitra' initiative, alongside Parent-Teacher Meetings (PTMs). To raise public awareness, 18-20 theatre troupes will be formed under the 'Seva Smaran' (Service Remembrance) initiative; these troupes will perform street plays in schools, colleges, and panchayats, with special performances scheduled for October 2, the release said. Furthermore, a three-day event titled 'Aangan ka Milan' (Gathering in the Courtyard) will be held at all Anganwadi centres from September 25 to October 7. This event will feature the honouring of Anganwadi and ASHA workers, interactions with beneficiary mothers, and recreational activities for children, alongside the dissemination of information regarding nutrition and health schemes, the release added. To highlight the positive changes brought about in people's lives by government schemes, district and state-level digital data banks will be created by compiling authentic reels and short videos under the 'Kahani Badlav Ki' (Story of Change) component. Additionally, 'Seva Jyoti Yatra' will feature foot marches, as well as bicycle and motorcycle rallies across the state and districts; volunteers from 'Mera Yuva Bharat' will participate in these events, culminating in a collective pledge for 'Viksit Bharat 2047' (Developed India 2047). As the nationwide 'Vadnagar to Varanasi (Jal, Jan, aur Seva Sankalp Yatra)' passes through Bihar, arrangements will be made for grand receptions, security, accommodation, and interactions with local beneficiaries at designated stopover points, the release noted. To foster public participation, 25 activities, including the cleaning of ponds and Chhath ghats, tree plantation, and sanitation drives, will be conducted under the 'Seva Mera Yogdan' (Service: My Contribution) initiative, ensuring visible, on-ground transformation at a minimum of two locations in every assembly constituency. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary reviews preparation for 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan' - ANI News
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary reviews preparation for ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan’ ANI | Updated: Sep 12, 2026 20:53 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna (Bihar) [India], September 12 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary chaired a high-level review meeting on Saturday at 'Samvad' in the Chief Minister Secretariat to oversee preparations for the upcoming 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan' and 'Seva Sankalp Evam Kayakalp Abhiyan'. The meeting was attended by Deputy Chief Ministers Vijay Kumar Choudhary and Bijendra Prasad Yadav, Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit, Principal Secretary to CM Deepak Kumar, Development Commissioner Mihir Kumar Singh, along with cabinet ministers and senior department officials. During the meeting, Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit presented a detailed roadmap of both campaigns. The 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan' will run from September 17 to October 17, featuring 13 major themes and citizen-centric programs. Highlights include 'Aashirwad Ka Diya'—a statewide festival of lights on September 17 across districts, blocks, and booths—and the 'Seva Kshetra' initiative, which will conduct 7-day drawing and speech competitions in schools from September 25 to October 1. Additional events under the month-long drive include street plays under 'Seva Smaran' showcasing 25 years of welfare initiatives of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, a 3-day Anganwadi engagement drive ('Aangan Ka Milan'), a short video campaign titled 'Kahani Badlav Ki' targeting 25 lakh public experiences, a torchlight rally ('Seva Jyoti Yatra'), and 'Vadnagar to Varanasi'—a holy water pilgrimage via motorcycle. A day-long 'Seva Setu' camp on October 6 will address pending public grievances across all blocks. Concurrently, the 'Seva Sankalp Evam Kayakalp Abhiyan' will run from September 17, 2026, to March 31, 2027. This initiative focuses on two core objectives: upgrading existing public infrastructure and building new community assets. Upgrades and repair work for public amenities—such as sanitation, painting, drinking water, and electricity—will be completed by November 30, 2028, while new asset construction will conclude by March 31, 2027. Addressing the officials, Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary emphasised that public service and community welfare remain the highest priorities of the state government. He instructed ministers and district officials to formulate a strict 30-day calendar via video conferences and ensure maximum public participation. Ahead of the upcoming festival season, the Chief Minister urged administration teams to execute cleanliness drives, tree plantation, blood donation camps, and painting of schools, health centres, and Anganwadis before Diwali. He further directed each Gram Panchayat to identify and execute 10 localised development schemes to systematically strengthen rural infrastructure. (ANI)

national_raw_news.title: 3 hours ago | National 146 BRICS nations unanimously adopted New Delhi Declaration on 1st day of BRICS Summit 2026
national_raw_news.content: BRICS nations have unanimously adopted the New Delhi Declaration on the First day of the BRICS Summit 2026, being held at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Prime Minister Narendra Modi proposed to adopt the declaration at the end of the session on the first day of the summit. In his closing remarks, the Prime Minister noted that the New Delhi Declaration adopted today provides a clear direction for the shared resolve of the member countries. He added that it is now their shared responsibility to translate these resolutions into tangible results. The Prime Minister said that today’s discussion makes it evident that the changing world cannot be steered by outdated institutions and underlined that reforms are essential in representation, responsiveness, and rule-making. Mr Modi said that the leaders also emphasised that the Global South must have equal participation in the development of future technologies and the rules governing them. He emphasised that the gap between decisions and their outcomes must be bridged through partnership and collective action. The Prime Minister also expressed his gratitude to the leaders for their valuable contributions, constructive spirit and commitment as the BRICS Chair. To mark the 20 years of BRICS, two commemorative postage stamps were also released by the leaders of the member countries on this occasion. Earlier in his opening remarks on the first day of the session, which was based on inclusive Global Governance and Strengthening Multilateralism, Mr Modi proposed a BRICS Continuity and Implementation Mechanism to ensure that the grouping’s institutional momentum is maintained despite the Chairship changing every year. In his opening remarks at today’s session of the BRICS Summit 2026, which is underway at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, Mr Modi said the mechanism would enable follow-up of all initiatives and outcomes through the Troika. The Prime Minister said BRICS countries will have to work on a new and ambitious agenda for the next 20 years. He said the process must begin with the grouping’s own working system. The Prime Minister also proposed to establish a Seafarers Emergency Support Network to connect the maritime authorities and diplomatic missions of relevant countries to facilitate assistance during difficult times. Mr Modi observed that seafarers make a massive contribution to global trade, yet they often find themselves lacking support during difficult times. Mr Modi said the time has come to translate the unity and consensus among BRICS countries into concrete outcomes on the global stage. He stressed that BRICS members respect one another and move forward through consensus. He said the grouping is not working against anyone, but is moving forward with the approach of taking everyone along. The Prime Minister described this year’s BRICS Summit as a historic milestone, noting that the grouping is celebrating its 20th anniversary this year. He said BRICS is at its coming-of-age moment and has established its distinct identity on the global stage over the past two decades. Mr Modi said India’s Chairship of BRICS is based on a people-centric and humanity-first approach. He said Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability have been India’s foremost priorities as Chair. Guided by these priorities, India has laid special emphasis on connecting BRICS cooperation directly with the common people. The Prime Minister noted that with this vision, more than 350 meetings were organised, and India had the privilege of welcoming delegations across nearly 30 cities in the country. In his address, the Prime Minister noted that the Global South stands in the front row of global crises but in the back row of decision-making. He emphasised transforming this ‘pyramid of privilege’ into a ‘platform of partnership’. In this context, the Prime Minister proposed to jointly formulate 10 proposals for global governance reform, aiming to shape them into a BRICS reform roadmap by the time of the next Summit. On the issue of reform in the United Nations Security Council (UNSC), the Prime Minister emphasised that reform of the UNSC can no longer be postponed and negotiations on this matter must be linked to a definite time frame and clear outcomes. He said, similarly, voting power, leadership positions, and policy priorities within financial institutions must align with today’s economic realities. national_raw_news.title: 3 hours ago | National 171 PM Modi holds bilateral talks with BRICS leaders
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President of China, Xi Jinping, today reaffirmed that India and China should take a strategic and long term perspective of their ties and differences should not become disputes. During their bilateral meeting on the sidelines of BRICS Summit in New Delhi, the two leaders welcomed the steady progress in India-China bilateral relations since their last meeting in Tianjin in August last year. Prime Minister highlighted that both sides must be guided by three mutuals- mutual respect, mutual sensitivity and mutual interest. He emphasized that peace and tranquility in the border areas remains an essential basis for the continued development of bilateral relations. He underlined the need for both sides to observe existing agreements and understandings on border related issues. The two leaders expressed commitment to a fair, reasonable, and mutually acceptable resolution of the boundary question proceeding from the political perspective of their overall bilateral relations and the long-term interests of the two peoples. External Affairs Ministry said in a statement that the two leaders took note of the progress in people-to-people ties and underscored the need to further promote cultural exchanges, business linkages and greater mobility between the two countries. On economic and trade relations, they underlined the need to address each other’s concerns, including structural trade imbalance and supply chain issues, and facilitation of meaningful and predictable market access. The two leaders agreed that both sides must continue to expand common ground on regional and global issues, and in addressing challenges. Earlier in the day, Prime Minister Modi held a series of bilateral meetings with his counterparts from Ethiopia, Malaysia and Vietnam as well as Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi on the sidelines of the Summit. The Prime Minister began his bilateral engagements by holding talks with his Ethiopian counterpart Dr Abiy Ahmed Ali. The Ministry of External Affairs said in a statement that the two leaders held discussions aimed at further strengthening the bilateral Strategic Partnership. Both the leaders reviewed progress across key sectors, including economic cooperation, defence and security partnership, and capacity building. The meeting built on Prime Minister Modi’s historic visit to Addis Ababa in December 2025. The two leaders also exchanged perspectives on regional and international developments of mutual interest and reaffirmed their commitment to close cooperation in multilateral fora. During the meeting, Prime Minister Modi expressed appreciation for Ethiopia’s participation in the 18th BRICS Summit and noted that its presence helped in reinforcing the collective voice of the Global South. The Prime Minister also held bilateral talks with his Malaysian counterpart Anwar Ibrahim. During the meeting, the two leaders reviewed the progress in bilateral cooperation across a range of areas, including trade and investment, defence and security and people-to-people ties. They also took stock of the outcomes of Prime Minister Modi’s visit to Malaysia in February this year. Mr Modi appreciated Malaysia’s continued support in strengthening ASEAN-India relations. The leaders exchanged views on key regional and global issues of mutual interest and expressed their continued commitment to advancing the India-Malaysia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. In the meeting with his Vietnamese counterpart Le Minh Hung, Prime Minister Modi welcomed Vietnam’s participation in the BRICS Summit as a Partner Country. The Ministry of External Affairs said that the meeting provided an opportunity for both leaders to review the progress made in bilateral ties, which were elevated to an Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership during the State Visit of Vietnamese President, To Lam to India in May this year. Both leaders also exchanged views on various regional and global issues of mutual importance, and reaffirmed the commitment to further strengthening their partnership. India and Vietnam share a time-tested friendship rooted in shared civilizational heritage, mutual trust and understanding. Vietnam is a key pillar of India’s Act East Policy and an important partner in India’s broader engagement with Southeast Asia. The Prime Minister also held bilateral talks with Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan. national_raw_news.title: India’s 2026 BRICS Presidency broadening historically strong oil-related ties with Gulf, says Report 2 hours ago 48
national_raw_news.content: India’s 2026 BRICS Presidency is broadening historically strong oil-related ties with the Gulf into a wider partnership spanning investment, technology, food security, clean energy and regional stability, a report has said. The report published in a daily published from UAE said energy ties remain the foundation of the relationship at the 18th BRICS Summit, but cooperation is expanding into new strategic areas. During Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to the UAE this year, both the countries deepened collaboration on crude oil, LNG and LPG, and agreed to increase UAE participation in India’s strategic petroleum reserves and explored strategic gas reserves. Another area of co-operation is food-security which can link Gulf demand with India’s agricultural and food-processing capabilities. Investment in storage, logistics and reliable supply chains can be explored, the report noted. Highlighting the timing of the event, the report said that regional tensions have renewed attention on energy security, maritime trade and safe shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, while Gulf states diversify their economies, invest in advanced technology and strengthen commercial links with Asia. The Gulf is represented in the expanded BRICS through Saudi Arabia and the UAE, providing the bloc greater weight in the global energy and finance landscape. India-Gulf ties grew stronger in February this year, when the country signed terms of reference with GCC and formally launched negotiations for a comprehensive free trade agreement, covering Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE.

national_raw_news.title: SEBI proposes changes to methodology for calculating expiry-day settlement prices of index and stock derivatives 2 hours ago 52
national_raw_news.content: Markets regulator SEBI on Saturday proposed changes to the methodology for calculating expiry-day settlement prices of index and stock derivatives, following a review of the newly introduced closing auction session (CAS) framework. In a consultation paper, SEBI proposed two options for determining the settlement prices, a blended Volume Weighted Average Price – VWAP based on trades executed during the last 30 minutes of the continuous trading session – CTS, and the 10-minute CAS, or continuation of the existing CTS VWAP methodology. The proposals follow feedback received from market participants on the use of the CAS-determined closing price for settling derivative contracts on expiry. Determination of derivative settlement prices based on the closing price arrived at through CAS was among the significant areas of feedback received by SEBI. SEBI introduced the CAS framework in the equity cash segment from August 3 to determine the closing price of securities. Under the current framework, the closing price determined through CAS also serves as the basis for determining settlement prices of derivative contracts on expiry. The use of the CAS-determined closing price for expiry-day settlement of derivatives has been one of the key concerns raised by market participants, prompting Sebi to review the existing methodology. On 3rd September, SEBI had said it may propose changes to the methodology following the feedback and indicated that a consultation paper on the proposed framework was likely to be released in about a week. The proposed changes are aimed at addressing concerns around the use of the CAS-determined closing price as the basis for settling derivative contracts on expiry. The Securities and Exchange Board of India – SEBI has sought comments from stakeholders on the proposals till 3rd October.

national_raw_news.title: Inflows through FCNR-B reflect confidence in India’s macroeconomic fundamentals: RBI Governor 2 hours ago 48
national_raw_news.content: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra has said that inflows through the Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) [FCNR-B] and the other schemes have been ‘very robust’. In an interview with a private television channel, the RBI Governor said the strong inflows reflect confidence in India’s macroeconomic fundamentals and demonstrate the ability to attract foreign capital within a short period. On the surplus liquidity in the banking system, Malhotra said the Reserve Bank has enough tools at its disposal to manage liquidity and is prepared to use them as needed. He added that some of the surplus liquidity would be withdrawn over time through currency circulation, forex intervention and banks’ reserve requirements amid rising credit growth. Malhotra added that the central bank’s objective was to maintain appropriate liquidity conditions and keep the weighted average call rate aligned with the repo rate. The RBI Governor said the Monetary Policy Committee would reassess growth and inflation dynamics at its meeting next month amid rising prices of crude oil owing to the ongoing West Asia crisis. Sanjay Malhotra noted that the impact of higher crude prices on inflation would depend on the extent to which the increase is passed through to consumers. He said the government has to a great degree, absorbed and cushioned the shock; as a result, the Indian economy has weathered it well. On stronger-than-expected growth in the April to June quarter, the RBI Governor said it was not entirely surprising. He added that incoming corporate data was also pointing to firmer growth. The central bank saw no signs of overheating, including in consumption loans.

national_raw_news.title: Saragarhi Day observed in Punjab, tributes paid to martyrs of Battle of Saragarhi 3 hours ago 52
national_raw_news.content: In Punjab, on the occasion of Saragarhi Day today, tributes were paid to the martyrs of the Battle of Saragarhi at its memorial in Ferozepur. In Amritsar, Bhog of Akhand Path Sahib was performed at Saragarhi Gurdwara in the memory of 21 British-Indian Sikh soldiers. They gave their supreme sacrifice while fighting with 10,000 Afghan tribals to defend the Saragarhi Fort in Waziristan on September 12th, 1897. A state-level programme was organised at Ferozepur in which family members of the martyrs, army officers and a large number of people paid tribute to the brave soldiers. State Minister Gurmeet Singh Khudiyan honoured their family members on the occasion. The Battle of Saragarhi is an unprecedented battle in world military history. It was on this day, 129 years ago, when 21 brave Sikh soldiers under the leadership of Havaldar Ishar Singh of the Sikh Regiment fought to their last breath against the Afghan tribesmen in Samana village of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, presently in Pakistan. They killed hundreds of attacking tribesmen and foiled their attempts to capture the Saragarhi Fort. They were honoured with the highest Indian military bravery award of those days, the Indian Order of Merit. The award is presently equated to Paramvir Chakra.

national_raw_news.content: Institutions should ensure maximum participation of youth in Vikasit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue 2027: Varanasi Additional DM Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Institutions should ensure maximum participation of youth in Vikasit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue 2027: Varanasi Additional DM ANI | Updated: Sep 12, 2026 06:32 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Varanasi (Uttar Pradesh) [ India ], September 12 (ANI): My Bharat District Advisory Committee meeting of My Young India (MY Bharat) was held on Friday in the Vimarsh Auditorium of Sunbeam School in Varanasi . The meeting was chaired by Additional District Magistrate (Protocol), Varanasi District, Vinay Kumar Singh. Special emphasis was placed on connecting youth with nation-building, encouraging their talent, creativity, leadership skills, and innovation, and aligning them with the resolve for a Viksit Bharat 2047. In the meeting, Deputy Director, My Bharat Varanasi , Vikas Singh, gave a detailed presentation on Viksit Bharat Young Leaders 2027 through a presentation. The presentation provided information about the various stages of the Vikas Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue, the Vikas Bharat Quiz, the upcoming selection process, and the various tracks available for youth. Program Coordinator of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapeeth, Rahul, provided practical information to the institution representatives through a PowerPoint presentation regarding the registration process on the My Bharat portal, the process of generating referral codes, and the process of connecting youth to My Bharat. The meeting specifically discussed youth participation in the Vikas Bharat Quiz 2027. Youth aged 15 to 29 can participate in this quiz. The quiz is scheduled from August 17, 2026, to September 30, 2026. The quiz will consist of 20 questions, and participants will be given 10 minutes to complete it. Additional District Magistrate (Protocol) Vinay Kumar Singh, who chaired the meeting, urged the heads of institutions and representatives to disseminate information about VBYLD 2027 to eligible students and youth from their respective institutions and encourage as many students as possible to participate in the Viksit Bharat Quiz, so that more and more youth from Varanasi district can join this national initiative. Information was also shared at the meeting regarding the key tracks of the Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue 2027 – Viksit Bharat Challenge, Cultural Track, Design for Bharat, Hack for Social Cause, Youth Entrepreneurs Challenge, and Youth Parliament. The institutions present at the meeting were urged to disseminate information about the Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue 2027 to as many eligible youths as possible and to encourage interested students and youth to participate in this national initiative. Expressing gratitude for the cooperation of all the officers, heads of institutions and representatives present, the Deputy Director of Mera Yuva Bharat, Varanasi , appealed to the youth of the district to participate more and more in VBYLD 2027 and play their active role in building a developed India 2047. But its journey tells a story that winds from a small village enterprise to a shift in national policy. At the SARAS Aajeevika Mela 2026 in Gurugram, one such story stood on display: bamboo bags crafted by Vishakha Didi from Assam. In 2014, she joined a Self-Help Group (SHG) and revitalised her father-in-law’s bamboo craft enterprise with new designs. Government support and exhibitions helped her reach wider markets. She participated in the India International Trade Fair, 2025; her bamboo creations earned her ₹ 2 lakh in sales. Her journey captures a moment that turned a homegrown craft into a thriving enterprise. For generations, bamboo was closely linked with traditional livelihoods across communities, but an outdated regulatory barrier once held back its true economic potential. Under a British-era law, bamboo was classified as a tree, which made harvesting and transporting it unnecessarily cumbersome for the people who depended on it. In 2017, the government took a landmark step by removing bamboo from this classification, freeing it from restrictive forestry regulations. This forward-thinking reform opened the doors to greater innovation, entrepreneurship, and value addition in the bamboo sector. The importance of this move is now visible across the country, especially in the Northeast, where bamboo is driving employment, business, and innovation. One such example is fashion designer and sustainable innovator Chimi Ongmu Bhutia’s Lagstal Design Studio near Gangtok, Sikkim . This women-led manufacturing enterprise makes bamboo handicrafts, incense sticks, furniture, interior décor items, etc. Bamboo here moves beyond traditional craft into contemporary design and enterprise. Chimi’s story is part of a wider movement. In Tripura , Bijoy Sutradhar adopted technology to improve bamboo product manufacturing . In Nagaland , SHGs around Dimapur are adding value to bamboo-based food products , alongside local enterprises like Khorolo Creative Crafts producing furniture and handicrafts. Meanwhile, in Mizoram’s Mamit district , teams are advancing scientific cultivation through bamboo tissue culture and poly-house management . These examples point towards the bamboo sector becoming more diverse, innovative, and value-driven. A transformation of this scale requires more than skilled hands. It needs technology, processing facilities, training, and stronger market connections. This is where government support becomes important. The National Bamboo Mission focuses on cultivation, processing, and market access for bamboo farmers, manufacturers, and sellers. It also supports nurseries for quality planting material . national_raw_news.title: First-ever PIB press tour for Arunachal media concludes at Statue of Unity
national_raw_news.content: Echo Of Arunachal Newsflash State News First-ever PIB press tour for Arunachal media concludes at Statue of Unity EKTA NAGAR (GUJARAT), Sep 11: The first-ever Press Information Bureau (PIB) press tour for media representatives from Arunachal Pradesh concluded on Friday at Ekta Nagar, Gujarat, with a visit to the Statue of Unity and the Sardar Sarovar Dam. The nine-member media delegation visited the Statue of Unity, the world’s tallest statue, and the Sardar Sarovar Dam built across the Narmada River on the final day of the five-day exposure tour. The journalists paid floral tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and undertook a guided tour of the Statue of Unity complex, including the viewing gallery and other facilities. They also interacted with Additional Collector Narayan Madhu, who briefed them on the development of Ekta Nagar and various initiatives undertaken in the region. The visit also featured an interaction with members of the Rathwa tribal community, providing an opportunity for cultural exchange between Arunachal Pradesh and Gujarat. The Arunachal journalists participated in traditional dances with members of the Rathwa community and exchanged greetings by presenting traditional scarves from Arunachal Pradesh. The five-day tour provided the delegation with exposure to Gujarat’s development initiatives across various sectors. The journalists visited the Dholera Greenfield Smart City, Sabarmati Multimodal Transport Hub, GIFT City and AMUL, gaining firsthand insights into developments in smart infrastructure, transportation, finance, technology and the dairy cooperative sector. The delegation also experienced Gujarat’s cultural heritage through participation in a traditional Garba performance. The tour provided the Arunachal media delegation with an opportunity to gain broader perspectives on India’s development journey while facilitating cultural interaction between the Northeast and western India. The exposure visit concluded with the delegation carrying back experiences and insights from Gujarat’s initiatives in infrastructure, technology, industry, cooperative development and cultural heritage.
